clusters.label: Control & Agency
clusters.root_question: Does it matter what I do?

clusters.label: Deservingness & Guilt
clusters.root_question: Am I allowed to have this?

clusters.label: Judgment & Comparison
clusters.root_question: Where do I stand relative to others?

clusters.label: Attachment & Outcome
clusters.root_question: Can I let this matter without gripping it?

clusters.label: Authenticity & Self-Expression
clusters.root_question: Am I allowed to be who I actually am?

entries.script: I am fundamentally flawed, and if people saw the real me, they'd leave.
entries.recognition: Over-editing yourself before anyone has reacted; relief that feels like getting away with something.
entries.reframe: I can be fully seen and still be someone worth staying for.

entries.script: I have to earn the right to take up space.
entries.recognition: Apologizing before making a request; shrinking in rooms where you weren't asked to.
entries.reframe: My presence doesn't require a receipt.

entries.script: My mistakes are proof of who I really am underneath.
entries.recognition: One error erases a long record of competence in your own mind within seconds.
entries.reframe: A mistake is something I did, not something I am.

entries.script: If I stop achieving, I stop mattering.
entries.recognition: Guilt during rest; identity that only stabilizes mid-task.
entries.reframe: What I do adds to my life. It was never the source of my worth.

entries.script: I'm too much, or not enough — never the right amount.
entries.recognition: Constant self-adjustment mid-conversation; exhaustion from calibrating.
entries.reframe: I get to find out what the right amount of me actually is, instead of guessing.

entries.script: I have to be perfect for anyone to actually value me.
entries.recognition: Rewriting messages a dozen times before sending; catastrophizing tiny errors in front of others.
entries.reframe: People value me for being real, not for being flawless.

entries.script: Compliments are just politeness; the criticism is what's true.
entries.recognition: Praise deflected instantly, criticism replayed for days.
entries.reframe: Both are data. Neither one gets to be the only truth automatically.

entries.script: If I show I'm struggling, people will see me as weak.
entries.recognition: Performing competence even while falling apart privately.
entries.reframe: Showing a struggle is showing I'm human, not showing I've failed.

entries.script: I'm only lovable when I'm useful to someone.
entries.recognition: Over-functioning in relationships; discomfort just receiving without giving something back immediately.
entries.reframe: I can be loved simply for being here, not only for what I provide.

entries.script: Deep down, I'm an impostor who hasn't been caught yet.
entries.recognition: Attributing success to luck or timing, never to skill; waiting for the “reveal.”
entries.reframe: What I've built is real, even on the days it doesn't feel like it.

entries.script: No one would notice if I disappeared.
entries.recognition: Testing this passively — going quiet to see who reaches out.
entries.reframe: My impact on people is often invisible to me. That's not the same as absent.

entries.script: I have to hide my real opinions to keep people close.
entries.recognition: Agreement that arrives faster than the actual thought did.
entries.reframe: The people who are actually mine can hold the real me.

entries.script: Real connection is for other people, not for me.
entries.recognition: Watching closeness from the outside, cataloguing it as a category you're excluded from.
entries.reframe: I haven't found my people yet. That's a location problem, not a worth problem.

entries.script: If I need someone, I've already lost.
entries.recognition: Refusing help even when it's offered freely; pride mistaken for independence.
entries.reframe: Needing someone is just being human in front of them.

entries.script: Being different means being alone.
entries.recognition: Sanding down the parts of yourself that don't match the room.
entries.reframe: What makes me different is also what makes me findable.

entries.script: If people really knew me, they'd be disappointed.
entries.recognition: Performing a curated version of yourself even with close friends.
entries.reframe: The version of me that gets tired, or gets it wrong, is still someone worth knowing.

entries.script: I have to be the one who reaches out, or the relationship dies.
entries.recognition: Silent resentment while continuing to initiate every single time.
entries.reframe: I can test what the relationship holds without carrying all of it myself.

entries.script: Everyone already has their people; there's no room for me.
entries.recognition: Assuming groups are closed before actually approaching them.
entries.reframe: Groups reshape more often than they look like they do from outside.

entries.script: If I set a boundary, I'll lose the relationship.
entries.recognition: Saying yes long after you mean no, to avoid a rupture that hasn't actually been tested.
entries.reframe: A relationship that can't survive a boundary was already this fragile before I set it.

entries.script: I have to agree with the group to stay in it.
entries.recognition: Laughing at things that don't land, nodding along past the point of honesty.
entries.reframe: The group I actually belong in can hold a different opinion from me.

entries.script: Nothing I do will change how this turns out.
entries.recognition: Giving up early, disguised as being realistic.
entries.reframe: I can't control the outcome, but I'm not as powerless inside it as this feels.

entries.script: The world is fundamentally unsafe, and I have to stay braced for it.
entries.recognition: A body that never fully exhales; scanning rooms for threat that isn't there.
entries.reframe: I can meet what comes without pre-living it first.

entries.script: Hope is just a setup for disappointment.
entries.recognition: Pre-emptively lowering expectations to soften a blow that hasn't happened.
entries.reframe: I can want something fully and still be alright if it doesn't arrive.

entries.script: Bad things happen to me more than to others.
entries.recognition: A running tally of misfortune that only counts confirming evidence.
entries.reframe: I'm noticing what fits the story. There's more happening than the tally shows.

entries.script: I have to control every outcome or something will go wrong.
entries.recognition: Over-preparing to the point of exhaustion; inability to delegate.
entries.reframe: I can hold things loosely and still be someone who handles what comes.

entries.script: If I relax, something will sneak up on me.
entries.recognition: An inability to fully rest even on objectively calm days.
entries.reframe: I can notice real signals without keeping every system on alert.

entries.script: Trusting someone is how you get hurt.
entries.recognition: Withholding trust as a blanket policy rather than assessing it person by person.
entries.reframe: Trust can be given in proportion to what someone's actually shown me.

entries.script: If I'm not the one holding it together, everything falls apart.
entries.recognition: Refusing to delegate even small, low-stakes tasks.
entries.reframe: Things can hold together without me being the only load-bearing wall.

entries.script: The safest choice is always the smallest one.
entries.recognition: Defaulting to the option that risks the least, regardless of what you actually want.
entries.reframe: Safety and smallness aren't always the same choice.

entries.script: Something bad happening once means it will happen again.
entries.recognition: Treating a single past event as a permanent forecast.
entries.reframe: One data point isn't a pattern yet.

entries.script: My effort doesn't actually move the needle.
entries.recognition: Quiet quitting on projects that once mattered; going through motions.
entries.reframe: I might not see the effect yet. That's different from there being none.

entries.script: Other people, or circumstances, decide how my life goes.
entries.recognition: Describing your own choices in passive voice — “it happened,” not “I chose.”
entries.reframe: Within real constraints, there's still a next choice that's mine.

entries.script: There's no point starting something I might not finish perfectly.
entries.recognition: Unfinished drafts, unopened first pages, ideas that never leave the notebook.
entries.reframe: A finished, imperfect thing beats a perfect thing that never existed.

entries.script: I only have power over small things, never the big ones.
entries.recognition: Dismissing your own influence as trivial before testing it.
entries.reframe: Big things are usually just small things, repeated.

entries.script: Trying and failing is worse than never trying.
entries.recognition: Choosing not to enter the arena so the loss stays hypothetical.
entries.reframe: An honest attempt teaches me something a hypothetical never will.

entries.script: If I ask for help, it means I've failed at this.
entries.recognition: Struggling silently through something a request would resolve in minutes.
entries.reframe: Asking for help is a move I make, not a verdict on my competence.

entries.script: The system is too big for one person to affect.
entries.recognition: Opting out of participation because the scale feels disproportionate to any single action.
entries.reframe: I don't need to move the whole system to move my part of it.

entries.script: If I set a plan, I have to follow it exactly or I've failed.
entries.recognition: Abandoning an entire project the moment reality diverges from the original outline.
entries.reframe: A plan is a starting direction, not a contract I'm bound to.

entries.script: Waiting for the right moment is the responsible thing to do.
entries.recognition: Perpetual preparation that never converts into a first, imperfect step.
entries.reframe: The right moment is usually made by starting, not found by waiting.

entries.script: I can't change now — I've already gone too far down this path.
entries.recognition: Continuing a choice mainly because reversing it would mean admitting the old one was wrong.
entries.reframe: Distance already traveled doesn't obligate me to keep traveling it.

entries.script: This feeling outside me is the only thing that will fill what's missing.
entries.recognition: Chasing the next acquisition, relationship, or high the moment the last one settles.
entries.reframe: What I want is pointing me somewhere real. It isn't the whole destination.

entries.script: Wanting this much means something is wrong with me.
entries.recognition: Shame layered on top of ordinary appetite; secrecy about simple wants.
entries.reframe: Wanting is information, not a verdict on my character.

entries.script: Once I have it, the ache will finally stop.
entries.recognition: The goalpost quietly moving the instant it's reached.
entries.reframe: This will feel good. It won't be the last thing I ever want, and that's fine.

entries.script: Pleasure now always costs me later.
entries.recognition: Guilt that arrives on schedule, regardless of the actual consequence.
entries.reframe: Some pleasure is simply pleasure. I can check the actual cost instead of assuming one.

entries.script: What I truly want isn't allowed.
entries.recognition: Wanting in private, denying in public, a gap that grows over years.
entries.reframe: I can find out what's actually true for me before I decide what's allowed.

entries.script: If I get what I want, I'll feel guilty for wanting it.
entries.recognition: Sabotaging the very outcome you worked toward once it's within reach.
entries.reframe: I can want something, get it, and simply enjoy that it happened.

entries.script: My appetite for life is bigger than is appropriate.
entries.recognition: Shrinking your presence, your laugh, your hunger for experience to seem more manageable to others.
entries.reframe: A large appetite for living isn't a defect to manage down.

entries.script: Craving something means I lack self-control.
entries.recognition: Moralizing ordinary desire as a personal failing.
entries.reframe: A craving is a signal, not a character flaw.

entries.script: If I chase what excites me, I'm being selfish.
entries.recognition: Routinely deprioritizing your own excitement in favor of what looks responsible to others.
entries.reframe: What excites me is often exactly what I have something real to offer from.

entries.script: Desire fades once you actually have the thing, so wanting is pointless.
entries.recognition: Pre-emptively devaluing a goal to protect against future disappointment.
entries.reframe: Some desire settles into satisfaction. That's not proof the wanting was pointless.

entries.script: I am only as valuable as my last result.
entries.recognition: A win that produces relief instead of joy — you dodged something instead of gaining something.
entries.reframe: My last result was one thing I did. It's not a referendum on me.

entries.script: Rest has to be earned by output.
entries.recognition: Inability to enjoy downtime without a mental ledger running underneath.
entries.reframe: Rest is part of the work, not a reward that comes after it.

entries.script: If I'm not the best, I've failed.
entries.recognition: Comparison that erases genuine progress the moment someone else is faster.
entries.reframe: Getting better than I was is its own complete win.

entries.script: Slowing down means falling behind for good.
entries.recognition: Pushing through depletion because stopping feels like losing ground permanently.
entries.reframe: A pause is a position, not a collapse.

entries.script: My worth is measured by what I've built, not who I am.
entries.recognition: Introducing yourself with your résumé before your name settles in the room.
entries.reframe: What I've built came from who I already am — not the other way around.

entries.script: If it comes easily, it doesn't really count.
entries.recognition: Discounting natural strengths, only crediting the things that cost visible struggle.
entries.reframe: Something being easy for me doesn't make it worth less.

entries.script: There's always a next level I haven't reached yet, so I can't be satisfied now.
entries.recognition: The goalpost resetting the instant a milestone is hit, with no pause to register it.
entries.reframe: I can register this milestone fully before the next one starts.

entries.script: Other people's success shrinks what's available for mine.
entries.recognition: Quiet competitiveness even with people who aren't in your actual arena.
entries.reframe: Their success and mine aren't drawing from the same pool.

entries.script: I have to prove myself again with every new person or room.
entries.recognition: Re-establishing credentials from scratch in every new context, as if none of it carries over.
entries.reframe: What I've already proven doesn't reset every time the audience changes.

entries.script: Ambition and contentment can't coexist.
entries.recognition: Treating satisfaction as a threat to drive, so you manufacture dissatisfaction to keep moving.
entries.reframe: I can want more and be genuinely glad about where I already am.

entries.script: Nothing I care about will matter in the end anyway.
entries.recognition: Caring quietly withdrawn from things before they're finished, to soften a loss in advance.
entries.reframe: Meaning doesn't require permanence to be real while it's happening.

entries.script: It's safer to want nothing than to want something and lose it.
entries.recognition: Flat affect substituted for real preference; “I don't care” as armor.
entries.reframe: I can want things and still survive not getting all of them.

entries.script: This is just how my life is going to be.
entries.recognition: Treating the current chapter as the whole book.
entries.reframe: This is how my life is right now. Right now isn't a life sentence.

entries.script: Caring deeply is naive.
entries.recognition: Cynicism worn early, before disappointment has actually happened, as pre-emptive protection.
entries.reframe: Caring is a risk I can choose to take with open eyes, not a mistake I haven't made yet.

entries.script: I already know how this story ends for me.
entries.recognition: Foreclosing possibility before the evidence is in — certainty standing in for fear.
entries.reframe: I don't actually know the ending. That's uncomfortable, and also where the freedom is.

entries.script: If I can't see the whole picture, none of the pieces matter.
entries.recognition: Abandoning meaningful small actions because they don't add up to something obviously large.
entries.reframe: A piece can matter completely without me seeing the whole picture yet.

entries.script: Ordinary life isn't enough; only something extraordinary would justify being here.
entries.recognition: Dismissing quiet, daily satisfactions as not counting toward a “real” life.
entries.reframe: An ordinary day can hold real meaning without needing to be extraordinary.

entries.script: If it doesn't last forever, it wasn't really worth it.
entries.recognition: Devaluing a relationship, job, or season retroactively once it ends.
entries.reframe: Something can matter completely and still have an ending.

entries.script: I have to find my one true purpose before I'm allowed to commit to anything.
entries.recognition: Staying uncommitted for years, waiting for a single calling to reveal itself.
entries.reframe: I can commit to what excites me now and let purpose clarify as I go.

entries.script: Wanting things to feel meaningful is naive; life is mostly neutral facts.
entries.recognition: Flattening genuine wonder into detached commentary, as a form of self-protection.
entries.reframe: Meaning is something I get to notice and build, not something I have to prove exists first.

entries.script: I don't deserve good things unless I've suffered for them.
entries.recognition: Discomfort with ease; unconsciously creating hardship to “earn” an outcome that was already freely available.
entries.reframe: I can receive good things because I exist, not because I paid for them first.

entries.script: If something good is happening, it must be about to end.
entries.recognition: Bracing during good moments instead of being in them; a reflexive “too good to be true.”
entries.reframe: A good moment doesn't come with a clock I have to watch.

entries.script: I have to keep feeling bad before I'm allowed to move on.
entries.recognition: Rehearsing an apology internally long after it's been given and accepted.
entries.reframe: I can take full responsibility and still let the guilt end when the repair is done.

entries.script: Wanting more than I already have is greedy.
entries.recognition: Downplaying desires the moment they're spoken aloud; pre-emptive self-correction.
entries.reframe: Wanting more is often just growth, asking for room.

entries.script: Pleasure has to be earned through hardship first.
entries.recognition: The “no pain, no gain” reflex applied to things that were never actually a struggle.
entries.reframe: Some things can simply be easy. Ease isn't proof that I cheated.

entries.script: I have to apologize for taking up someone's time.
entries.recognition: Opening requests with pre-emptive guilt rather than a clear ask.
entries.reframe: My time and theirs are both simply real. Neither needs an apology attached.

entries.script: If I say no, I owe an elaborate explanation.
entries.recognition: Over-justifying a boundary as if “no” alone were insufficient.
entries.reframe: A complete sentence can be a complete answer.

entries.script: Success I didn't struggle for isn't really mine.
entries.recognition: Crediting circumstance or luck for anything that arrived without a fight.
entries.reframe: Ease doesn't disqualify something from being genuinely mine.

entries.script: I have to prove I've suffered enough before I'm allowed to feel better.
entries.recognition: Staying in a low mood past its natural point, as if leaving early would be dishonest.
entries.reframe: Feeling better doesn't require a permission slip made of enough pain first.

entries.script: I don't get to feel proud of myself; that's for other people to decide.
entries.recognition: Waiting for external validation before allowing any internal satisfaction.
entries.reframe: I can be the one who decides whether I did well.

entries.script: Where they are proves where I should be by now.
entries.recognition: Measuring your own timeline against someone else's highlight reel.
entries.reframe: Their pace is information about them. Mine is information about me.

entries.script: If I judge it first, it can't hurt me.
entries.recognition: Pre-emptive criticism of people or ideas before actually engaging with them.
entries.reframe: I can stay open without staying unprotected.

entries.script: Being further along means being better.
entries.recognition: Quiet hierarchy-building — ranking people, including yourself, by stage, status, or speed.
entries.reframe: Different stages aren't different worth. They're just different stages.

entries.script: If I can't do it as well as they can, I shouldn't do it at all.
entries.recognition: Avoiding beginner status entirely; quitting the moment visible competence isn't already there.
entries.reframe: Everyone who's good at this started exactly where I am.

entries.script: Other people's choices are a verdict on mine.
entries.recognition: Feeling threatened or judged by someone simply living differently than you do.
entries.reframe: Their path running doesn't put mine on trial.

entries.script: If I don't have an opinion on everything, I look uninformed.
entries.recognition: Manufacturing a stance under social pressure rather than admitting “I don't know yet.”
entries.reframe: Not having an opinion yet is a legitimate position, not a gap to hide.

entries.script: Someone disagreeing with me means one of us is wrong.
entries.recognition: Treating differing views as a contest with a single correct winner.
entries.reframe: Two people can see the same thing differently without either one being wrong.

entries.script: The way I was raised to see the world is simply how the world is.
entries.recognition: Mistaking an inherited framework for an observed fact.
entries.reframe: What I was taught to see is a lens. I can look at what's actually there.

entries.script: If someone corrects me, it means they think less of me.
entries.recognition: Hearing feedback as a verdict on your worth rather than information about one thing you did.
entries.reframe: A correction is about the thing, not about me.

entries.script: I have to be right to be respected.
entries.recognition: Doubling down on a position after realizing it's wrong, to avoid losing face.
entries.reframe: Changing my mind in view of better information is one of the most respectable things I can do.

entries.script: It only counts if it happens exactly the way I pictured it.
entries.recognition: Dismissing a genuinely good outcome because it didn't match the original mental picture.
entries.reframe: I can hold a clear direction and still let the path surprise me.

entries.script: If I stop pushing for this outcome, it won't happen.
entries.recognition: White-knuckling a goal long after the joy has left the process.
entries.reframe: I can act fully toward what I want without gripping the how.

entries.script: A different outcome than the one I wanted means I failed.
entries.recognition: Labeling redirection as defeat before you've seen where it actually leads.
entries.reframe: A different outcome is still an outcome. It hasn't been graded yet.

entries.script: I have to know how this ends before I can start.
entries.recognition: Stalling indefinitely at the planning stage, waiting for a certainty that isn't coming.
entries.reframe: I can start with a direction and let the destination clarify as I move.

entries.script: Everything happens for a fixed reason I'm not allowed to question.
entries.recognition: Passivity disguised as acceptance; using fate as a reason to avoid a hard choice.
entries.reframe: I can treat this moment as open, and choose, rather than already written.

entries.script: If I let go of the outcome, I'll stop caring altogether.
entries.recognition: Gripping tightly out of fear that loosening equals indifference.
entries.reframe: I can care completely and hold the outcome loosely at the same time.

entries.script: A slower path than expected means I'm behind.
entries.recognition: Measuring your timeline against an imagined schedule that was never guaranteed.
entries.reframe: The pace it's actually taking is the pace it's actually taking.

entries.script: If this doesn't work out, it will have been for nothing.
entries.recognition: Erasing everything gained along the way the moment a goal isn't reached.
entries.reframe: What I gained on the way there doesn't disappear if the destination changes.

entries.script: I need a guarantee before I'm willing to commit.
entries.recognition: Waiting indefinitely for certainty that no real commitment ever actually comes with.
entries.reframe: I can commit fully to something whose outcome I don't yet know.

entries.script: Wanting a specific result too much will jinx it.
entries.recognition: Performing detachment as superstition rather than as genuine ease.
entries.reframe: Wanting something clearly doesn't have power over whether it arrives.

entries.script: There's never enough time for the things that actually matter.
entries.recognition: Chronic rushing paired with an inability to name what the rush is actually protecting.
entries.reframe: There's enough time for what I actually make room for.

entries.script: If I slow down now, I'll never catch up.
entries.recognition: Treating rest as a debt that compounds instead of a reset.
entries.reframe: Catching up assumes a race that may not be the one I'm actually running.

entries.script: There isn't enough to go around, so someone else's gain is my loss.
entries.recognition: Discomfort at others' success, even in areas completely unrelated to your own.
entries.reframe: Someone else doing well doesn't use up my share.

entries.script: I'm running out of time to become who I was supposed to be.
entries.recognition: Age-based panic detached from any actual deadline.
entries.reframe: Who I'm becoming doesn't have a closing date.

entries.script: Money is the one resource I can never fully trust to be there.
entries.recognition: Hoarding, over-checking balances, anxiety disproportionate to the actual numbers.
entries.reframe: I can build a real relationship with money instead of a fearful one.

entries.script: Being wealthy would make me a worse person.
entries.recognition: Unconsciously capping your own income or opportunities to avoid an imagined moral cost.
entries.reframe: What I do with resources says more about me than having them does.

entries.script: If it didn't require struggle, it isn't a real accomplishment.
entries.recognition: Manufacturing difficulty for its own sake, distrusting anything that comes easily.
entries.reframe: Ease doesn't disqualify an accomplishment from being real.

entries.script: There's a fixed amount of good fortune in the world, and I've likely used mine up.
entries.recognition: Treating a run of good luck as something that must now be “owed back.”
entries.reframe: Good fortune isn't a ledger I can overdraw.

entries.script: I should already be further along financially than I am.
entries.recognition: Measuring your finances against an arbitrary timeline borrowed from someone else's life.
entries.reframe: Where I am financially is where I am. That's a starting point, not a verdict.

entries.script: Enjoying money means I'm not serious about my values.
entries.recognition: Feeling guilty for spending on pleasure even when it's well within your means.
entries.reframe: Enjoying what I have is compatible with everything I actually value.

entries.script: If I don't hustle constantly, opportunity will pass me by for good.
entries.recognition: Treating every pause as an irreversible loss of momentum.
entries.reframe: Opportunity tends to be more abundant, and more repeatable, than the panic suggests.

entries.script: Needing more time than others is a personal failing.
entries.recognition: Comparing your pace to an average that was never actually promised to apply to you.
entries.reframe: The time something takes me is just the time it takes me.

entries.script: The unfamiliar is dangerous until proven otherwise.
entries.recognition: Reflexive no to new people, foods, routes, or ideas — before any actual assessment.
entries.reframe: Unfamiliar isn't the same as unsafe. I can find out which this is.

entries.script: If I change, I'll lose the people who loved the old version of me.
entries.recognition: Staying small in relationships to avoid disrupting a familiar dynamic.
entries.reframe: The people who are actually mine can grow alongside me.

entries.script: Once I decide who I am, I'm not allowed to become someone else.
entries.recognition: Clinging to an old identity years after it stopped fitting.
entries.reframe: I get to keep updating who I am. That was always allowed.

entries.script: Uncertainty means something is wrong.
entries.recognition: Treating the discomfort of not-knowing as a problem to solve immediately, rather than a phase to move through.
entries.reframe: Uncertainty is just the shape of a threshold. It isn't a verdict.

entries.script: Starting over means everything before it was wasted.
entries.recognition: Staying in the wrong job, place, or relationship to protect the time already sunk into it.
entries.reframe: What came before taught me something. It doesn't have to be repaid with more of the same.

entries.script: If I don't recognize who I've become, something's gone wrong.
entries.recognition: Treating growth-driven change in yourself as alarming rather than expected.
entries.reframe: Not recognizing an old version of myself can be a sign of movement, not malfunction.

entries.script: The plan has to survive contact with reality unchanged, or the plan failed.
entries.recognition: Treating any deviation from the original plan as proof the whole thing was flawed.
entries.reframe: A plan that adapts is doing exactly what plans are for.

entries.script: If I don't know the next step, I shouldn't take this one.
entries.recognition: Needing the entire staircase visible before agreeing to climb the first stair.
entries.reframe: I can take the step I can see and trust the next one will appear closer up.

entries.script: Choosing differently than I did before means my old choice was wrong.
entries.recognition: Defending a past decision indefinitely to avoid implying you've grown past it.
entries.reframe: A new choice can be right for who I am now without the old one being wrong for who I was then.

entries.script: New information that contradicts what I believed means I was foolish to believe it.
entries.recognition: Treating updated understanding as embarrassing rather than as the system working correctly.
entries.reframe: Updating what I believe when I learn more is exactly what a healthy mind does.

entries.script: I have to hide the parts of myself that make people uncomfortable.
entries.recognition: Monitoring your own reactions in real time to keep them palatable to whoever's in the room.
entries.reframe: The parts of me that make some people uncomfortable are often exactly what makes me real to the right ones.

entries.script: I must follow the path my family expects, or I'll lose their love.
entries.recognition: Making major life decisions by first asking what would be approved of, not what's true.
entries.reframe: I can honor where I came from and still choose where I'm going.

entries.script: Being myself is fine in private, but not safe to bring into the world.
entries.recognition: A public self and a private self that have grown far apart from each other.
entries.reframe: I can bring more of my private self into the open, a little at a time, and see what actually happens.

entries.script: I have to match the group's opinions to be accepted by it.
entries.recognition: Sensing the room's consensus before forming your own view, then adopting it as if it were yours.
entries.reframe: The group that's actually mine can hold my honest view too.

entries.script: Loving myself openly would come across as arrogant.
entries.recognition: Undercutting your own accomplishments in conversation before anyone else can.
entries.reframe: Genuine self-respect and arrogance aren't the same thing, and other people can usually tell the difference.

entries.script: If I stop performing the role people expect, they'll be disappointed in who's actually there.
entries.recognition: Maintaining a persona long after it stopped matching how you actually feel.
entries.reframe: The people who matter are responding to a role. They deserve the chance to meet who's actually here.

entries.script: Following someone else's proven path is safer than trusting my own direction.
entries.recognition: Copying a life template because it worked for someone else, ignoring the mismatch with your own excitement.
entries.reframe: Someone else's path can be information. It doesn't have to be my instructions.

entries.script: I have to justify my choices to people who didn't ask for an explanation.
entries.recognition: Pre-emptively defending decisions nobody has actually challenged.
entries.reframe: My choices can simply be mine, without a defense attached.

entries.script: My partner could easily find someone better than me.
entries.reframe: Being chosen doesn't require being the best option on paper.

entries.script: My body isn't good enough to be seen.
entries.reframe: My body can be seen as it is, today.

entries.script: I'll never live up to what my parents hoped for.
entries.reframe: Their hopes were theirs; I get to measure my life by my own.

entries.script: I have to keep giving to be worth keeping.
entries.reframe: I can be kept for who I am, not only for what I give.

entries.script: I only deserve rest after a productive day.
entries.reframe: Rest is part of how I work, not a reward for it.

entries.script: I'm only a good parent or child if I sacrifice myself.
entries.reframe: Taking care of myself is part of taking care of them.

entries.script: One bad review shows what I'm really like.
entries.reframe: One review shows one moment, not who I am.

entries.script: There's something about me that makes people pull away.
entries.reframe: People pull away for many reasons, most of them not about me.

entries.script: My ideas are strange; better to keep them in.
entries.reframe: Strange ideas are often the ones worth sharing.

entries.script: I was the difficult one, and that's just who I am.
entries.reframe: A role I had as a child is not who I have to be now.

entries.script: People can see straight away that I'm awkward.
entries.reframe: Most people are too busy with their own nerves to notice mine.

entries.script: Someone this good to me must be making a mistake.
entries.reframe: I can let someone be good to me without checking whether I've earned it.

entries.script: I don't deserve to be paid well for something I enjoy.
entries.reframe: Enjoying my work doesn't make it worth less.

entries.script: Taking care of my body is self-indulgent.
entries.reframe: Looking after my body is maintenance, not indulgence.

entries.script: My needs make life harder for my family.
entries.reframe: My needs are part of the family, not a weight on it.

entries.script: If I ask for what I need, I'm too much.
entries.reframe: Asking clearly is a gift to the people who love me.

entries.script: I shouldn't bother friends with my problems.
entries.reframe: Friends often feel closer when I let them help.

entries.script: Going to the doctor is making a fuss about nothing.
entries.reframe: Checking in on my health is ordinary care.

entries.script: Asking for a raise makes me difficult.
entries.reframe: Asking for fair pay is a normal part of work.

entries.script: Love has to be earned and can be taken away at any moment.
entries.reframe: Real love doesn't need to be re-earned every day.

entries.script: I was loved for being good, not for being me.
entries.reframe: I can learn to love the parts of me that weren't praised.

entries.script: People only like me for what I do for them.
entries.reframe: Some people like me for who I am; I can let them show it.

entries.script: I'll be lovable once I look different.
entries.reframe: I can be loved in the body I have now.

entries.script: The real me isn't lovable.
entries.reframe: The real me deserves the same kindness I give others.

entries.script: If I show my real work, people will lose interest in me.
entries.reframe: Showing real work tends to draw the right people closer.

entries.script: No one in my family really gets me.
entries.reframe: Being understood can come from more places than my family.

entries.script: I'm always the outsider on a team.
entries.reframe: Feeling outside can change when I let one person in.

entries.script: I'll end up alone.
entries.reframe: I don't know my future, and I can keep connecting today.

entries.script: I have to handle everything by myself.
entries.reframe: I can carry my part and let others carry some.

entries.script: Nobody would care about what I make.
entries.reframe: Someone out there is looking for exactly what I make.

entries.script: I have to look like the others to be taken seriously.
entries.reframe: My own way of working can earn respect too.

entries.script: I need to look a certain way to fit in.
entries.reframe: I can fit in somewhere as I am, and some places aren't worth fitting into.

entries.script: I have to earn and spend like my circle does.
entries.reframe: My money choices can follow my own values.

entries.script: My style is too different to be accepted.
entries.reframe: A different style is how people find me.

entries.script: If we argue, the relationship is in danger.
entries.reframe: Disagreement can make a relationship stronger.

entries.script: Saying no to my boss will cost me my place.
entries.reframe: A clear, respectful no is part of being reliable.

entries.script: If I live my own way, my family will turn away.
entries.reframe: My family may need time, and I can live my way meanwhile.

entries.script: If I'm honest about how I feel, friends will drift off.
entries.reframe: Honesty shows me which friendships are real.

entries.script: Everyone notices when I make a mistake.
entries.reframe: Most people forget my mistakes long before I do.

entries.script: People are judging how I look.
entries.reframe: Most people are thinking about themselves, not about me.

entries.script: If it isn't praised, it isn't any good.
entries.reframe: My work can be good before anyone says so.

entries.script: What I earn tells people what I'm worth.
entries.reframe: Income measures a job, not a person.

entries.script: My parents' approval decides whether I did well.
entries.reframe: I can decide for myself whether I did well.

entries.script: I can't feel good about a choice until someone confirms it.
entries.reframe: I can trust a choice before anyone else signs off on it.

entries.script: My body could fail me at any moment.
entries.reframe: My body is doing a lot right, every day.

entries.script: Getting close means getting hurt.
entries.reframe: Closeness carries risk, and also everything I'm looking for.

entries.script: One mistake and I'll lose everything.
entries.reframe: Mistakes are usually survivable and often fixable.

entries.script: One unexpected bill could ruin me.
entries.reframe: I can build some buffer and handle surprises step by step.

entries.script: If I'm open, people will take advantage.
entries.reframe: I can be open and still keep healthy limits.

entries.script: I have to protect my family from everything.
entries.reframe: I can protect what I can and trust them with the rest.

entries.script: Good news at work never lasts.
entries.reframe: Good news can simply be good news.

entries.script: Every ache is the start of something serious.
entries.reframe: Most aches pass; I can check what needs checking.

entries.script: This relationship will end like the others did.
entries.reframe: This relationship is new information, not a rerun.

entries.script: Just when money is fine, something will go wrong.
entries.reframe: Things going well is not a warning sign.

entries.script: If I finally finish it, it will flop.
entries.reframe: Finishing teaches me more than any flop could cost.

entries.script: Better to stay in the job I know than risk one I'd love.
entries.reframe: I can explore what I'd love without leaping blindly.

entries.script: Sharing my work is too exposing.
entries.reframe: Sharing one small piece is a safe first step.

entries.script: Wanting less means getting hurt less.
entries.reframe: Wanting openly is how I find what fits.

entries.script: I should never take a financial risk, however small.
entries.reframe: Small, considered risks are part of growing.

entries.script: Standing out draws the wrong kind of attention.
entries.reframe: Standing out also draws the right people.

entries.script: Changing career at my age is reckless.
entries.reframe: Change can be planned and tested before it's a leap.

entries.script: If the relationship changes, it's breaking.
entries.reframe: Relationships change shape to stay alive.

entries.script: If my routine changes, I'll fall apart.
entries.reframe: I can adapt more than I think, one day at a time.

entries.script: Things at home should stay the way they've always been.
entries.reframe: A family can change and still be home.

entries.script: I'm too old to change how I am.
entries.reframe: People change at every age, often in small steps.

entries.script: Good partners are rare; I'd better hold on to this one.
entries.reframe: I can stay because it's right, not because of scarcity.

entries.script: There are only so many good jobs, and others will get them first.
entries.reframe: Opportunities keep appearing for people who keep showing up.

entries.script: All the good ideas are already taken.
entries.reframe: My version of an idea has never been made.

entries.script: My health is all genes; nothing I do matters.
entries.reframe: Genes set a range; my choices still move within it.

entries.script: I'll always struggle with money; it's how I'm made.
entries.reframe: Money habits can be learned, like any other skill.

entries.script: I just attract the wrong people.
entries.reframe: I can notice patterns in who I choose and choose differently.

entries.script: That's how my family is; nothing will change.
entries.reframe: I can change how I take part, even if they don't change.

entries.script: If I don't organise everything, home falls apart.
entries.reframe: Others can carry parts of home too, in their own way.

entries.script: I need to know exactly where this relationship is going.
entries.reframe: I can enjoy where it is while it unfolds.

entries.script: If I miss one workout, the whole plan is ruined.
entries.reframe: One missed day is just one day.

entries.script: If I delegate, it won't be done right.
entries.reframe: Done differently is often done well enough.

entries.script: If it ends, the whole relationship was a waste.
entries.reframe: Something can end and still have been worth it.

entries.script: If it doesn't sell, it wasn't worth making.
entries.reframe: Making it was already part of the reward.

entries.script: My job is just a way to pay the bills; it can't mean anything.
entries.reframe: I can find something that matters in parts of my work.

entries.script: I'll be happy once I get the promotion.
entries.reframe: I can find satisfaction on the way, not only at the top.

entries.script: Once I have enough money, I'll finally relax.
entries.reframe: I can practise relaxing at the money level I have now.

entries.script: When I find the right person, I'll feel complete.
entries.reframe: I can feel whole on my own and share that with someone.

entries.script: When I'm fitter, I'll start doing what I love.
entries.reframe: I can start doing what I love in the body I have.

entries.script: When my family approves, I can choose freely.
entries.reframe: I can choose freely now and let approval follow or not.

entries.script: I'll start living once the timing is right.
entries.reframe: Right now is the only timing I have to work with.

entries.script: When I'm more talented, I'll start creating.
entries.reframe: Creating is how talent grows.

entries.script: When people finally see me, I'll feel okay.
entries.reframe: I can see myself first.

entries.script: If I'm not busy, I'm wasting my life.
entries.reframe: An empty hour can be exactly what the day needed.

entries.script: A day off has to be productive to count.
entries.reframe: A day off counts by being off.

entries.script: I can't rest while others still need something.
entries.reframe: Someone always needs something; I can still rest.

entries.script: Taking a sick day lets the team down.
entries.reframe: Resting when I'm ill is how I stay reliable.

entries.script: Everyone else is getting more done than me.
entries.reframe: I'm comparing my inside to their highlight reel.

entries.script: If they ask for my time, I should give it.
entries.reframe: My time is mine to offer, not owed.

entries.script: Saying no to extra work will be held against me.
entries.reframe: A clear no now protects the yes I've already given.

entries.script: If I stop for a moment, everything piles up.
entries.reframe: Things pile up whether I stop or not; stopping helps me meet them.

entries.script: Being bored means something is wrong.
entries.reframe: Boredom is often the doorway to the next real interest.

entries.script: If I start crying, I won't be able to stop.
entries.reframe: Tears come in waves, and waves end.

entries.script: My anger will push people away.
entries.reframe: Anger said calmly tells people where I stand.

entries.script: Feeling angry makes me a bad person.
entries.reframe: Anger is a signal that something matters to me.

entries.script: Showing emotion at work is unprofessional.
entries.reframe: Naming a feeling briefly can be the most professional thing in the room.

entries.script: My sadness is too heavy for other people.
entries.reframe: People can choose how much they can hold; I can let them choose.

entries.script: Anxiety means something bad is about to happen.
entries.reframe: Anxiety is my body getting ready, not a forecast.

entries.script: If I feel too happy, I'll pay for it later.
entries.reframe: Joy isn't a loan I have to repay.

entries.script: It's safer not to get too excited.
entries.reframe: Excitement is information, not a jinx.

entries.script: In my family, we don't talk about feelings.
entries.reframe: I can be the first one to say a feeling out loud.

entries.script: If my partner is upset, I've done something wrong.
entries.reframe: Their mood can be theirs without being my fault.

entries.script: Feeling jealous means I'm a small person.
entries.reframe: Jealousy points at something I want; I can look at it.

entries.script: I should be able to control how I feel.
entries.reframe: I can't choose every feeling; I can choose what I do with it.

entries.script: I should feel bad for a long time after I mess up.
entries.reframe: Guilt has done its job once I've repaired what I can.

entries.script: My body is something to fight.
entries.reframe: My body is on my side, even on hard days.

entries.script: Getting older means everything goes downhill.
entries.reframe: Aging changes things; it doesn't only take things away.

entries.script: After a certain age, people stop seeing you.
entries.reframe: I can keep showing up and being seen at any age.

entries.script: My body is just how it is now; nothing will improve.
entries.reframe: Small changes in movement, sleep and food still add up.

entries.script: I have to deserve food before I can enjoy it.
entries.reframe: Eating is care, not a reward.

entries.script: My body shouldn't need this much care.
entries.reframe: Needing care is what bodies do.

entries.script: I can't trust my body to cope with pressure.
entries.reframe: My body has handled pressure many times; I can help it settle.

entries.script: I have to look younger to stay relevant.
entries.reframe: Relevance comes from what I bring, not my age.

entries.script: Feeling pleasure in my body is embarrassing.
entries.reframe: Enjoying my body is ordinary and private to me.

entries.script: I should push through pain rather than complain.
entries.reframe: Pain is information; I can listen and act.

entries.script: I'm failing my kids.
entries.reframe: Good-enough parenting is what kids actually need.

entries.script: My children should never feel unhappy.
entries.reframe: Kids learn resilience from feelings I let them have.

entries.script: Every mistake I make will scar my children.
entries.reframe: Repair after a mistake teaches them more than perfection would.

entries.script: A good parent puts themselves last.
entries.reframe: A rested parent is a better parent.

entries.script: When the kids leave home, I'll be left with nothing.
entries.reframe: My life can grow new rooms when theirs moves on.

entries.script: I don't know who I am apart from being a parent.
entries.reframe: I was someone before, and I can find them again.

entries.script: Choosing differently from my parents is betraying them.
entries.reframe: I can love them and still live differently.

entries.script: I'm responsible for keeping the peace at home.
entries.reframe: Peace isn't my job alone.

entries.script: My parents' wishes come before mine.
entries.reframe: I can weigh their wishes and still choose.

entries.script: Everyone eventually goes.
entries.reframe: Some people go, and some stay; I can't know which yet.

entries.script: If they don't text back, they're losing interest.
entries.reframe: A late reply is usually about their day.

entries.script: If I have to ask for it, it doesn't count.
entries.reframe: Asking clearly helps people love me well.

entries.script: When it really matters, I'm on my own.
entries.reframe: I can check who has shown up before; the list may surprise me.

entries.script: Nobody ever really looked after me, so nobody will.
entries.reframe: What I lacked then doesn't fix what's possible now.

entries.script: If I'm kind, I'll be taken for granted.
entries.reframe: Kindness with limits is still kindness.

entries.script: People are nice to me only when they want something.
entries.reframe: Some niceness is just niceness; I can tell by what follows.

entries.script: If I lend or share, I'll be taken advantage of.
entries.reframe: I can share what I'm fine losing and say no to the rest.

entries.script: Keeping the peace matters more than what I want.
entries.reframe: Real peace includes my wants too.

entries.script: My partner's mood decides my day.
entries.reframe: I can care about their mood and still have my own day.

entries.script: Saying "I love you" first is too risky.
entries.reframe: Saying it first is a gift, not a gamble.

entries.script: I shouldn't draw attention to myself.
entries.reframe: Being seen is how the right people find me.

entries.script: My ideas are probably obvious; someone must have thought of them already.
entries.reframe: Obvious to me isn't obvious to everyone.

entries.script: If I succeed, I'll leave others behind.
entries.reframe: My success can lift others too.

entries.script: If I do well, my friends will resent me.
entries.reframe: Real friends can be glad for me.

entries.script: Doing better than my parents feels disloyal.
entries.reframe: Doing well can honor what they gave me.

entries.script: Posting my work online means inviting judgment.
entries.reframe: Posting invites response, and most of it is quieter than I fear.

entries.script: Being nervous means I'm not good enough.
entries.reframe: Nerves mean this matters to me.

entries.script: If I can't do it brilliantly, I shouldn't put my name on it.
entries.reframe: My name can stand on honest, finished work.

entries.script: If it isn't perfect, it doesn't count.
entries.reframe: Done teaches more than perfect ever will.

entries.script: Lowering my standards would make me mediocre.
entries.reframe: Flexible standards are still standards.

entries.script: A 95% result is basically a failure.
entries.reframe: 95% is a great result I'm allowed to enjoy.

entries.script: Being hard on myself is what keeps me in line.
entries.reframe: Kindness keeps me going longer than harshness does.

entries.script: People who mess up deserve to feel bad.
entries.reframe: People, me included, change faster with repair than with blame.

entries.script: My home has to look perfect before people can come over.
entries.reframe: People come for me, not the house.

entries.script: I need someone to tell me what to do.
entries.reframe: I can make a choice, learn from it, and adjust.

entries.script: I'm hopeless with practical things like money and forms.
entries.reframe: Practical things are learnable, one step at a time.

entries.script: If my manager leaves, I'll be lost.
entries.reframe: I know more than I give myself credit for.

entries.script: I need the scroll, snack or drink just to feel okay.
entries.reframe: I can feel okay for a few minutes without it, and see.

entries.script: When it gets hard, I need to switch to a new project.
entries.reframe: The hard middle is where things get finished.

entries.script: Once I start, I can't stop.
entries.reframe: I can pause once, and that pause is mine.

entries.script: I always mess up when it counts.
entries.reframe: I'm remembering the misses more than the hits.

entries.script: Everyone online is doing better than me.
entries.reframe: I'm seeing their edits, not their lives.

entries.script: If I don't keep checking, I'll miss something important.
entries.reframe: Important things tend to find me.

entries.script: One more video will make me feel better.
entries.reframe: What I actually need right now might be rest, or a person.

entries.script: If I'm not online, I'll be forgotten.
entries.reframe: The people who matter remember me offline too.

entries.script: I can't sit with my own thoughts.
entries.reframe: Five quiet minutes is something I can practise.

entries.script: Fun is for after the work is done.
entries.reframe: Fun can fuel the work.

entries.script: Playing just for the joy of it is childish.
entries.reframe: Play is how adults learn, too.

entries.script: Serious people don't chase what excites them.
entries.reframe: Excitement is a serious signal about where my energy is.

entries.script: Spending on joy is irresponsible.
entries.reframe: A little money spent on joy is part of a sane budget.

entries.script: When things are this good, I should brace.
entries.reframe: I can enjoy this moment without guarding it.

entries.script: Life should be easier than this; if it's hard, I'm doing it wrong.
entries.reframe: Hard is part of every real life, not proof I'm failing.

entries.script: It's safer to drift than to make a choice I might get wrong.
entries.reframe: Not choosing is also a choice; I'd rather make mine.

entries.script: My life is too ordinary to matter.
entries.reframe: Ordinary days are where most of life's meaning lives.

entries.script: Thinking about death means something is wrong with me.
entries.reframe: Thinking about endings can make today clearer.

entries.script: If I let myself love fully, losing them will destroy me.
entries.reframe: Grief is the cost of love, and people do survive it.

entries.script: Questioning what I was taught to believe makes me a bad person.
entries.reframe: Questioning is how beliefs become my own.

entries.script: If my work doesn't change the world, it's pointless.
entries.reframe: Changing one person's day is real change.

entries.script: I'll know my purpose once I find the right path.
entries.reframe: Purpose shows up as I follow what pulls me, step by step.

entries.script: Friendships always fade eventually.
entries.reframe: Some friendships fade and some deepen; I can tend the ones I want.

entries.script: If I need them too much, they'll leave.
entries.reframe: Needing someone is part of being close.

entries.script: It's safer not to get attached.
entries.reframe: Attachment is how I get to be close; I can survive its risks.

entries.script: Good colleagues always move on, so why invest?
entries.reframe: People who move on can still stay in my life.

entries.script: Needing someone is weakness.
entries.reframe: Needing people is how humans are built.

entries.script: If I don't do it, nobody will.
entries.reframe: Other people can pick things up if I let them.

entries.script: If I tell people how I feel, they won't really listen.
entries.reframe: Some people listen well; I can find and choose them.

entries.script: When I'm ill, I'll have to manage on my own.
entries.reframe: I can let people help when I'm unwell.

entries.script: People are there for the good times, not the hard ones.
entries.reframe: I can find out who shows up by letting them see the hard times.

entries.script: If the team is stressed, I have to carry it.
entries.reframe: I can support the team without holding all of it.

entries.script: If a friend is having a hard time, I have to drop everything.
entries.reframe: I can be there and still keep my own life going.

entries.script: Other people's moods are my responsibility.
entries.reframe: Their moods are theirs; my kindness is mine.

entries.script: It's not my place to ask for what I want.
entries.reframe: Asking is how people know what I want.

entries.script: I don't really know what I want anyway.
entries.reframe: I can find out what I want by noticing what pulls me.

entries.script: Spending on myself is selfish when others need things.
entries.reframe: Meeting my own needs is part of being able to give.

entries.script: My free time belongs to whoever needs it.
entries.reframe: Some of my time is just mine.

entries.script: My ideas aren't as important as other people's.
entries.reframe: My ideas deserve a turn too.

entries.script: I need my friends to agree before I decide.
entries.reframe: I can hear them and still decide for myself.

entries.script: I'm whoever the people around me need me to be.
entries.reframe: I can be someone of my own, with them.

entries.script: My job is who I am.
entries.reframe: My job is something I do, not all that I am.

entries.script: Family will take whatever I give and ask for more.
entries.reframe: I can give what feels right and stop there.

entries.script: If I trust people, I'm naive.
entries.reframe: Trust can be given in steps, and taken back if needed.

entries.script: Everyone has a hidden agenda.
entries.reframe: Most people are mostly what they seem.

entries.script: If I share my ideas, someone will steal them.
entries.reframe: Sharing ideas usually brings more ideas back.

entries.script: I have to seem fine around other people.
entries.reframe: I can be honest about a hard day without making it a scene.

entries.script: I'll fall apart if my family isn't there to help.
entries.reframe: I have more strength than I've had to use yet.

entries.script: If something goes wrong with my health, I won't cope.
entries.reframe: I can take things one step at a time and ask for help.

entries.script: Strong feelings will overwhelm me.
entries.reframe: Strong feelings rise and fall; I can wait them out.

entries.script: I don't have what it takes to do something original.
entries.reframe: Original work starts with trying, not with talent proven in advance.

entries.script: Unless I do the full workout, it's not worth doing.
entries.reframe: Ten minutes of movement counts.

entries.script: If my finances aren't fully sorted, I've failed.
entries.reframe: Getting a little more organised is real progress.

entries.script: If I make a mistake at work, I should never forget it.
entries.reframe: I can learn from it and let it go.

entries.script: If I eat badly, I have to make up for it.
entries.reframe: One meal doesn't need to be paid back.

entries.script: If my partner messes up, they should feel it.
entries.reframe: We can repair things instead of keeping score.

entries.script: Work that feels like play isn't real work.
entries.reframe: Enjoying my work often makes it better.

entries.script: Relationships are supposed to be hard work, not fun.
entries.reframe: Play and lightness keep love alive.

entries.script: Moving just for fun is a waste of time.
entries.reframe: Moving for joy is as good for me as moving for fitness.

entries.script: Hobbies are a luxury I can't afford.
entries.reframe: Something I love doing is part of a well-run life.

entries.script: Being too cheerful makes people take me less seriously.
entries.reframe: Joy and seriousness can live in the same person.

entries.script: Following what excites me is irresponsible.
entries.reframe: Following what excites me, responsibly, is how I find my direction.

entries.script: Every new ache could be something serious.
entries.reframe: Most aches pass; I can get the worrying ones checked.

entries.script: If I switch off completely, something will go wrong.
entries.reframe: Switching off is how I recharge to handle things.

entries.script: I can't start until I feel like it.
entries.reframe: I can start before I feel ready; the feeling often follows.

entries.script: I have to become a better version of me before I can accept this one.
entries.reframe: I can accept who's here and keep growing from here.

entries.script: If I can't do it yet, I'm just not good at it.
entries.reframe: “Not yet” is a stage, not a verdict.

entries.script: Unless I reach my full potential, I'm wasting my life.
entries.reframe: Potential is an invitation, not a debt.

entries.script: I have to sort myself out inside before I can really start living.
entries.reframe: I can live fully while I'm still working things out.

entries.script: The people I admire are a different kind of person from me.
entries.reframe: The people I admire started out ordinary and built their skill and belief over time.

entries.script: I'm not allowed to try this until I'm formally qualified.
entries.reframe: I can learn by doing, and get qualified along the way if it's needed.
entries.source: Blueprint p.209–210; Koch, Unreasonable Success (make your own trail)

entries.script: I have to fix my weaknesses before I can succeed.
entries.reframe: Building on my strengths can take me further than patching every weakness.

entries.script: I don't have any real standout strength.
entries.reframe: I may have a strength I overlook because it comes so easily.

entries.script: One big setback means I'm not cut out for this.
entries.reframe: Setbacks show up in almost every success story; they can be fuel.

entries.script: Feeling afraid means I'm weak.
entries.reframe: Fear is information about what matters to me, not a verdict on me.
entries.source: Bashar online, The Hidden Truth about Fear (Channelya summary)

entries.script: Money only counts if I worked hard for it.
entries.reframe: Money can come from value, help, timing or ease, and still be honest money.

entries.script: If I'm not outworking everyone, I'm a slacker.
entries.reframe: What I contribute counts, not how many hours I log.

entries.script: Being exhausted proves I worked hard enough.
entries.reframe: Tiredness tells me about my energy, not about my value.

entries.script: Handing off what I'm bad at is lazy.
entries.reframe: Letting others do what they do better frees me for my best work.

entries.script: Sleep is wasted time I could be using.
entries.reframe: Sleep is how my mind and body get ready for what's next.

entries.script: If I lose interest in something, something's wrong with me.
entries.reframe: Interests change as I change; that's information, not a flaw.

entries.script: If I feel stuck or keep struggling, it's all my own failing.
entries.reframe: Feeling stuck says something about the situation and my next step, not about my worth.

entries.script: If I look too closely at myself, I'll find something terrible.
entries.reframe: What I find up close is usually more workable than it looks from a distance.

entries.script: If I don't experience what others describe, something's wrong with me.
entries.reframe: People experience things differently; that's variety, not a defect.

entries.script: Asking someone more experienced to teach or back me is imposing.
entries.reframe: Many people enjoy passing on what they know, and asking for a champion is normal.
entries.source: Blueprint p.210; Koch, Unreasonable Success (attract a mentor)

entries.script: Contacting someone I barely know for help is imposing.
entries.reframe: Loose contacts are often glad to help, and they open doors my close circle can't.

entries.script: Wanting recognition for my work makes me needy.
entries.reframe: Wanting recognition is human, and it helps keep belief going.

entries.script: If I can't do the big dream yet, the small steps aren't worth it.
entries.reframe: Small steps on the real thing are the big dream, in progress.

entries.script: If I'm on the right path, I shouldn't have doubts.
entries.reframe: Doubt comes with anything that matters; I can doubt and keep going.

entries.script: If I still feel bad sometimes, I'm going backwards.
entries.reframe: Hard feelings are part of growing, not proof it failed.

entries.script: If an old pattern shows up again, all my progress was fake.
entries.reframe: Catching an old pattern sooner is what change looks like.
entries.source: transcript list #140; Blueprint p.12, p.113, p.169–170; Masters ch.8

entries.script: When I have two good options, I have to pick the one right one.
entries.reframe: Both options can be good; choosing one shows me which fits.

entries.script: I should be good at everything, not just one or two things.
entries.reframe: Being excellent at a few things beats being average at all of them.

entries.script: To change, I have to fight and defeat the old me.
entries.reframe: The old me was protecting something; I can thank it and choose differently.

entries.script: If I own my part in how I reacted, I'm letting them off the hook.
entries.reframe: Owning my response is about my freedom, not about who was right.

entries.script: Taking responsibility means admitting it's all my fault.
entries.reframe: Owning my part is about what I can do next, not about blame.

entries.script: When bad things happen to me, it's what I deserve.
entries.reframe: Hard things happen to everyone; they aren't a sentence handed to me.

entries.script: In the end, I'll have to pay for everything I did wrong.
entries.reframe: I can repair what I can now; I don't have to live waiting for a final verdict.

entries.script: When something goes wrong, someone has to be blamed.
entries.reframe: Things can go wrong without a culprit; I can look for the fix instead.

entries.script: I was born in the wrong place; I'd belong somewhere else.
entries.reframe: I can build belonging where I am, and still explore elsewhere.

entries.script: What I'd really love to do would look silly to other people.
entries.reframe: Things that look silly from outside often matter most from inside.

entries.script: Success has to look the way everyone says it should.
entries.reframe: I can define success in a way that fits my life.

entries.script: If I talk about my unusual experiences, people will think I'm crazy.
entries.reframe: I can choose whom to tell; some people will be curious, not dismissive.

entries.script: If no one else is doing it, it's probably a bad idea.
entries.reframe: An empty path can mean an open opportunity, not a mistake.
entries.source: Koch, Unreasonable Success (make your own trail)

entries.script: If everyone else stays late, I should too.
entries.reframe: I can set my hours by what works, not by what the office does.

entries.script: I have to defend who I am against every criticism.
entries.reframe: Criticism is information I can weigh; who I am doesn't need defending.

entries.script: If enough people say it about me, it must be true.
entries.reframe: Repetition isn't proof; I can check what people say against what I know.

entries.script: When people comment on what I do, it's usually a dig at me.
entries.reframe: Most comments are neutral; I can ask before assuming.

entries.script: I need everyone to like me.
entries.reframe: I can put my energy into the people who matter most to me.

entries.script: Every opportunity I get, I have to create myself.
entries.reframe: Some doors open from the other side; I can notice them and walk through.

entries.script: Lucky breaks and unexpected help don't happen to me.
entries.reframe: Help sometimes comes from directions I didn't plan; I can learn to notice it.
entries.source: Bashar online, Simple Way to Understand Law of Abundance (Channelya summary)

entries.script: If I can't help someone I love, I've failed.
entries.reframe: Being there counts, even when I can't fix it.

entries.script: I must never let anyone down.
entries.reframe: Letting someone down now and then is the price of being honest about my limits.

entries.script: Stepping back from a friendship that drains me makes me a bad person.
entries.reframe: I can step back from what drains me and still be kind.

entries.script: I can't go after what I want without someone getting hurt.
entries.reframe: Many of the things I want can be had without anyone losing.

entries.script: If I lose someone, I lose part of who I am.
entries.reframe: What they gave me stays part of me.

entries.script: If I really join a group, I'll lose myself in it.
entries.reframe: I can belong and still be fully me; good groups need me to be.

entries.script: If I speak up against the people in charge, I'll be punished.
entries.reframe: I can disagree respectfully, and learn which places can handle it.

entries.script: Strangers and people very different from me are probably a threat.
entries.reframe: Different isn't the same as dangerous; I can let people show me who they are.
entries.source: Blueprint p.233, p.281, p.284; Masters ch.3

entries.script: Without a steady paycheck, I'd end up with nothing.
entries.reframe: I can plan a change so a gap in income is survivable.

entries.script: Worrying is how I stay prepared.
entries.reframe: Worry doesn't steer events; preparing, acting, or deciding not to act does.
entries.source: Blueprint p.284; Koch, Boing Boing interview 2011

entries.script: If something seems too good to be true, it is.
entries.reframe: Some good things are simply good; I can check the facts instead of assuming a catch.

entries.script: If I let myself be as capable as I really am, it would be too much to handle.
entries.reframe: I can grow into my strength one step at a time.

entries.script: What I love doing can't pay the bills.
entries.reframe: I can test, in small ways, whether what I love can earn something.
entries.source: Blueprint p.156–158, p.168; Koch, The 80/20 Principle

entries.script: An okay life is the most I can expect.
entries.reframe: I'm allowed to aim for more than okay.

entries.script: I should only set goals I'm sure I can reach.
entries.reframe: A stretching goal can pull more out of me than a safe one, even if I fall short.
entries.source: Koch, Unreasonable Success (Olympian expectations, distort reality)

entries.script: Believing I could do something exceptional is arrogant.
entries.reframe: Belief in what I could contribute can serve other people, not just me.

entries.script: Putting everything into one thing is too risky.
entries.reframe: Focusing on the one thing I'm best placed for can be the smarter bet.

entries.script: Letting go of old beliefs would mean betraying who I was.
entries.reframe: I can thank an old belief for what it did and still put it down.

entries.script: A rule that once kept me safe must still be needed.
entries.reframe: What protected me then can be retired now.

entries.script: Real change only happens after everything falls apart.
entries.reframe: Change can be small and deliberate; it doesn't need a crisis.

entries.script: If I stop believing this, something bad will happen.
entries.reframe: I can try a different belief for a week and see what actually happens.

entries.script: I should only take on work I already know how to do.
entries.reframe: Stretching into the unfamiliar is how rare skills get built.

entries.script: A big shake-up in my life can only set me back.
entries.reframe: An upheaval can also be where I learn the most.

entries.script: I have to be there for everything, or I'll miss out.
entries.reframe: I can't be everywhere; where I am gets my full attention.

entries.script: I have to say yes to every opportunity that excites me.
entries.reframe: Saying no to most opportunities leaves room for the few that fit me.
entries.source: transcript list #149; Koch, The 80/20 Individual (vital few)

entries.script: Money is the only real support I can count on.
entries.reframe: Skills, trades, gifts, help and good timing are resources too.

entries.script: If I follow one interest, I'll have to give up all the others.
entries.reframe: One interest often opens the door to the others.

entries.script: Working together never really pays off; everyone has to look out for themselves.
entries.reframe: Cooperation often gets more done than going it alone.

entries.script: I can't be strong and vulnerable at the same time.
entries.reframe: Being able to show what I feel is part of strength.

entries.script: Admitting my doubts, even to myself, would make them stronger.
entries.reframe: Naming a doubt is the first step to checking it.

entries.script: I don't really have any fears worth looking at.
entries.reframe: Admitting a fear is how I get to work with it.

entries.script: I've already dealt with that, so it can't be what's driving this.
entries.reframe: I can look again; old things sometimes have deeper roots.

entries.script: My past decides who I am and what's possible for me.
entries.reframe: My past explains a lot; it doesn't get the final word.
entries.source: transcript list #54, #116, #164; Blueprint p.127–128; Masters ch.12

entries.script: Where I come from decides how far I can go.
entries.reframe: My background shapes my start, not my ceiling.
entries.source: Blueprint p.89, p.127; Koch, Unreasonable Success

entries.script: What happens decides how I feel; I get no say.
entries.reframe: Between what happens and how I feel, there's a reading I can check.
entries.source: transcript list #57, #113; Blueprint p.169; Masters ch.9

entries.script: If the obvious route is blocked, there's no way through.
entries.reframe: A blocked route usually means a different route.

entries.script: There's a ceiling on what someone like me can do.
entries.reframe: I don't know where my limits are until I test them.
entries.source: Blueprint p.8, p.11–12, p.88; Masters ch.5

entries.script: People don't really change.
entries.reframe: People change, usually slowly and in small ways.

entries.script: Real change takes years; it can't happen any faster.
entries.reframe: Some shifts happen the moment I see a belief clearly, and I can act like who I'm becoming today.
entries.source: Blueprint p.88, p.100, p.131; Bashar online, Mirror Mirror; Actualized.org forum

entries.script: What I really want can't happen in the life I have now.
entries.reframe: There's usually some version of it I can start right here.

entries.script: This pain, or this low mood, will never lift.
entries.reframe: Feelings that seem permanent still move, even before I can feel them moving.
entries.source: Blueprint p.194; Bashar online, Mirror Mirror

entries.script: My habits run on their own; I can't catch them in time.
entries.reframe: With practice I can notice the moment just before the habit.

entries.script: Once a doctor names it, my story is written.
entries.reframe: A diagnosis is important information; how I live with it is still partly mine.

entries.script: Self-confidence is something you're born with or not.
entries.reframe: Confidence can be built through experience and focus.

entries.script: Happiness comes down to luck or temperament; I can't plan for it.
entries.reframe: I can notice what made me happy before and make more room for it.

entries.script: I'm stuck with whoever life happens to put around me.
entries.reframe: I can choose where I put my time with people.

entries.script: My chances depend on who I already know.
entries.reframe: New people, even passing contacts, can open doors I can't predict.

entries.script: Small amounts of money will never add up to much.
entries.reframe: Small amounts, kept up over time, can grow more than I'd guess.

entries.script: I've already done everything I can to improve my life.
entries.reframe: There's usually a bigger improvement available than I can see from here.

entries.script: I can only relax once everything is taken care of.
entries.reframe: Something will always be open; I can rest with loose ends.

entries.script: Being strong means having the upper hand over other people.
entries.reframe: Real strength doesn't need anyone else to be smaller.

entries.script: The only way to change something is to fight against it.
entries.reframe: I can put my energy into building what I want, not only fighting what I don't.
entries.source: Blueprint p.35, p.154, p.244; Masters ch.7

entries.script: If people were free to decide for themselves, everything would fall apart.
entries.reframe: People often handle freedom better than I expect.

entries.script: If it hasn't happened by now, it isn't going to.
entries.reframe: Late isn't the same as never.

entries.script: If I follow what excites me, it should pay off.
entries.reframe: Following what excites me is worth it on its own; results come in their own form and time.

entries.script: If I start something, I have to finish it.
entries.reframe: Stopping on purpose is a decision, not a failure.

entries.script: When something goes wrong, nothing good can come of it.
entries.reframe: I don't know yet what this leads to; I can look for what it makes possible.
entries.source: transcript list #22, #84; Blueprint p.54, p.97–99, p.146; Masters ch.9

entries.script: Losing my job means my life has gone wrong.
entries.reframe: Losing a job is hard, and it can also make room for the next thing.

entries.script: I took a wrong turn somewhere, and my life is off course.
entries.reframe: Wherever I am is a place I can choose from.

entries.script: One thing going wrong spoils the whole day.
entries.reframe: One bad moment is one moment; the day can still go well.

entries.script: The painful years of my life were simply wasted.
entries.reframe: Even the hard years left me something I can build on.

entries.script: Nothing really excites me, so there's nothing to follow.
entries.reframe: Quiet interest counts too; I can follow the faintest pull.

entries.script: Small pulls aren't worth acting on; only a big passion counts.
entries.reframe: The small thing that interests me now is a real step.
entries.source: Bashar online, Act on Your Highest Excitement (Channelya summary); Transcend with Celine

entries.script: I can't start until I have the money and everything else in place.
entries.reframe: I can start with what I have and gather the rest on the way.

entries.script: I can only be happy once the other person changes.
entries.reframe: I can change my part, whatever they do.

entries.script: I can't accept my life now until the past is put right.
entries.reframe: The past can stay unfinished while I live well now.
