entries.script: Someone will eventually come along and sort my life out.
entries.reframe: Help may come, and I can start sorting things myself now.

entries.script: I'll only believe in myself once I've seen the proof.
entries.reframe: Belief can come first; acting on it is often how the proof arrives.
entries.source: Blueprint p.84, p.87; Masters ch.5; Koch, Unreasonable Success

entries.script: I need a good reason before I'm allowed to feel happy.
entries.reframe: I can enjoy a moment without it having to earn its place.

entries.script: When I'm stuck, all I can do is wait for something to change.
entries.reframe: Feeling stuck is a cue to take one small step and look again.

entries.script: I can't enjoy life while it has this many limits.
entries.reframe: Every life has limits; I can find what's good inside mine.

entries.script: I can't really change while the people around me stay the same.
entries.reframe: I can change first; some people will follow and some won't.

entries.script: It's up to the people in charge to fix things, not me.
entries.reframe: I can't fix everything, but some of it is within my reach.

entries.script: Having more things will make me happier.
entries.reframe: Things give a lift; what lasts comes from how I spend my days.

entries.script: The best-paid option is always the right career move.
entries.reframe: A rare skill I enjoy can be a better guide than the pay.

entries.script: I can't trust my own sense of what's right for me.
entries.reframe: My sense of what pulls me is data I can test with small steps.

entries.script: Someone wiser than me holds the answers about how I should live.
entries.reframe: Wise people can inform me; I still get the final say about my life.
entries.source: Blueprint p.4, p.7, p.58, p.66, p.86–87

entries.script: If real success came, I couldn't handle it.
entries.reframe: I'd grow into success the way I've grown into other things.

entries.script: I shouldn't be happy while others are suffering.
entries.reframe: Being okay myself can make me more useful to people who aren't.

entries.script: Settling for less is what someone like me should expect.
entries.reframe: I'm allowed to want to be treated well.
entries.source: Bashar online, Podscan 2025-2026 episode; HubPages quote collection

entries.script: Earning a lot without long hours would be unfair.
entries.reframe: Being paid for the value I create, not my hours, is fair.

entries.script: If I don't like something, it has nothing to give me.
entries.reframe: Unpleasant things can still teach me or bring me something.

entries.script: Keeping busy is better than feeling what I feel.
entries.reframe: Feelings I let in tend to pass sooner than feelings I outrun.

entries.script: Fear is something to get rid of, not something to listen to.
entries.reframe: I can get curious about what the fear is pointing at.
entries.source: Blueprint p.283–284; Bashar online, The Hidden Truth about Fear

entries.script: If I let myself feel really good, it would be more than I could handle.
entries.reframe: I can get used to feeling good a little at a time.

entries.script: Pain is what's real; happiness is a fairy tale.
entries.reframe: Hard days and good days are both real; I don't have to discount the good ones.

entries.script: Making my own happiness a priority is selfish.
entries.reframe: Looking after my happiness makes me better for the people around me too.

entries.script: I have to be completely sure before I decide.
entries.reframe: Enough clarity for one step is enough to decide.

entries.script: I have to think everything through before I'm allowed to act.
entries.reframe: A small try often answers what more thinking can't.
entries.source: transcript list #47, #89, #91; Koch, The 80/20 Principle (decisions); Actualized.org forum

entries.script: If I analyse myself enough, I'll finally understand myself.
entries.reframe: I learn who I am more from doing than from analysing.

entries.script: I can't move on until I understand why it happened.
entries.reframe: I can move forward with some questions still open.

entries.script: I can't move on until they explain why they did it.
entries.reframe: I can close my own chapter without their reasons.

entries.script: I can only change once I know exactly where my patterns come from.
entries.reframe: Change can start before I know the whole backstory.

entries.script: I have to know exactly who I am before I can choose.
entries.reframe: I find out who I am by choosing.

entries.script: I can't trust anything I can't see or prove yet.
entries.reframe: I can act on a direction before all the evidence is in.

entries.script: I need to know what's coming to feel safe.
entries.reframe: I can feel steady without knowing what's next.

entries.script: My gut feeling isn't real evidence.
entries.reframe: Intuition built from experience is data I can check with a small step.
entries.source: Blueprint p.227, p.299; Koch, Unreasonable Success (unique intuition)

entries.script: I am my thoughts.
entries.reframe: I'm the one noticing my thoughts.

entries.script: I am what I feel.
entries.reframe: Feelings pass through me; I'm still here when they go.

entries.script: If something feels bad, it must be wrong.
entries.reframe: Feeling bad tells me something is hard, not that it's wrong.

entries.script: If I feel fear or resistance, it means I shouldn't do it.
entries.reframe: Fear and resistance can mean “wrong way” or just "new"; I can check which.

entries.script: If a belief feels familiar, it must be true for me.
entries.reframe: Familiar only means I've heard it often.

entries.script: The way I remember my past is simply what happened.
entries.reframe: Memory retells; I can look again at what it meant.

entries.script: If I feel incompetent, I must be.
entries.reframe: A feeling tells me about my state, not my ability.

entries.script: Being happy after a loss means I loved them less.
entries.reframe: Joy after loss can sit right next to love.
entries.source: transcript list #124, #125; Bashar online, Mirror Mirror

entries.script: If I let go of the pain, it's as if it never happened.
entries.reframe: The pain can soften while what happened still matters.

entries.script: If I let someone go, I lose our connection.
entries.reframe: I can let go of how it was and keep what we had.

entries.script: I'm not grieving the right way.
entries.reframe: There's no correct way to grieve; mine can look like mine.
entries.source: Grief Cognitions Questionnaire, Appropriateness of Grief subscale

entries.script: Accepting a gift makes me dependent.
entries.reframe: I can accept a gift and stay free.

entries.script: If I get something for free, I'm in their debt.
entries.reframe: A gift can be just a gift; thank you is enough.

entries.script: People will only help me once I've given them something first.
entries.reframe: Some people help simply because they want to.

entries.script: I can't accept a favour until I've paid it back.
entries.reframe: I can let some things simply be given.

entries.script: More hours always means more results.
entries.reframe: Past a point, extra hours cost more than they bring.

entries.script: Being busy means I'm making progress.
entries.reframe: Busy and useful aren't the same thing; I can check which this is.
entries.source: Koch, Living the 80/20 Way; The 80/20 Principle

entries.script: Everything on my list is equally important.
entries.reframe: A few things on my list carry most of the weight; I can start there.

entries.script: If it isn't working, I just need to push harder.
entries.reframe: When pushing stops working, changing the approach is often the stronger move.
entries.source: transcript list #13, #52, #88, #150; Koch, Boing Boing interview 2011; Masters ch.9

entries.script: Time spent thinking isn't real work.
entries.reframe: Thinking is often where the best work starts.
entries.source: Koch, Living the 80/20 Way (act less, think more)

entries.script: I just need better time management to sort my life out.
entries.reframe: Choosing what matters helps more than squeezing more into each hour.
entries.source: Koch, The 80/20 Principle; Boing Boing interview 2011

entries.script: A full life means a full schedule.
entries.reframe: A full life can have plenty of space in it.

entries.script: The only way to make more money is to work harder and longer.
entries.reframe: Money can also grow from value, skill, timing and good choices, not only from more hours or more strain.
entries.source: Blueprint p.155–156, p.163; Koch, The 80/20 Principle

entries.script: If I work hard enough, I'll be rewarded fairly.
entries.reframe: Rewards follow value and position more than effort alone; I can choose where my effort goes.
entries.source: Koch, The 80/20 Principle; The Star Principle

entries.script: Life is a struggle; anything worth having has to be fought for.
entries.reframe: Some good things come through ease, not only through fighting.
entries.source: Blueprint p.10, p.230; Bashar online, Law of Abundance (Channelya summary)

entries.script: If something sounds simple, it can't really work.
entries.reframe: Simple things can work; I can try one and see.

entries.script: Changing a habit is always a hard, uphill fight.
entries.reframe: Some habits shift more easily when I change the setup, not my willpower.

entries.script: If I start living fully again, I'm leaving them behind.
entries.reframe: I can take them with me into the life I build now.

entries.script: My body should be over it by now.
entries.reframe: Grief moves through the body at its own pace.

entries.script: People expect me to have moved on, so I should hide it.
entries.reframe: I can let the right people know it still hurts.

entries.script: Keeping busy is the only way to get through a loss.
entries.reframe: I can take breaks from busyness and let the grief have a little room.

entries.script: If my partner does something for me, I have to even it out straight away.
entries.reframe: Love doesn't keep score, and I don't have to either.

entries.script: Accepting help from family means they'll hold it over me.
entries.reframe: I can accept help and still choose my own way.

entries.script: Receiving a compliment makes me uncomfortable, so I wave it away.
entries.reframe: I can let a compliment land and simply say thank you.

entries.script: If someone supports my work, I have to repay them before I can enjoy it.
entries.reframe: Support can be a gift I build on, not a debt I carry.

cores.belief: I'm not enough as I am.
cores.preferred: I'm enough to begin, and I can grow from here.
cores.protects: the risk of trying and being found lacking
cores.costs: never starting, or never feeling finished
rules: If I'm not the best, I'm nothing special.
I should be further along by now.

cores.belief: I have to earn my worth.
cores.preferred: My worth is a given; what I do is how I express it.
cores.protects: being judged as lazy or useless
cores.costs: rest that never comes, and a worth that resets every day
rules: If I'm not productive, I'm lazy.
If I rest, I fall behind.

cores.belief: Something is wrong with me.
cores.preferred: I have rough edges, not a broken core.
cores.protects: hoping, and then being rejected for who I am
cores.costs: hiding, so nobody gets to meet the real you
rules: If people see my mistakes, they'll see what's wrong with me.
I should keep the real me out of sight.

cores.belief: I don't deserve good things.
cores.preferred: Good things can come to me without a price paid in suffering.
cores.protects: having something good and losing it
cores.costs: pushing good things away before they can be taken
rules: If something good happens, I should wait for the catch.
I should only have good things after I've paid for them.

cores.belief: My needs are a burden.
cores.preferred: My needs are as normal as anyone's, and I can say them out loud.
cores.costs: help you'd gladly get, and people who'd like to be let in
rules: If I ask, I'm imposing.
I should handle it myself first.

cores.belief: If people really knew me, they wouldn't love me.
cores.preferred: The people who matter can know me and stay.
cores.costs: love that only ever reaches the edited version
rules: If they really knew me, they'd go.
I should show only the parts people like.

cores.belief: I don't belong anywhere.
cores.preferred: I can find and build places where I belong.
cores.protects: reaching out and not being met
cores.costs: staying on the edge of groups you'd like to be in
rules: If I reach out, I'll be ignored.
I should wait to be invited.

cores.belief: I have to fit in to be accepted.
cores.preferred: I can be different and still be accepted by the right people.
cores.protects: standing out and being pushed out
cores.costs: a life shaped by what others expect
rules: If I'm different, I'll be pushed out.
I should think what the group thinks.

cores.belief: If I'm fully myself or say no, people will leave.
cores.preferred: Honest relationships can hold my no and my truth.
cores.costs: swallowed no's and relationships built on half of you
rules: If I say no, I'll lose them.
I should keep the peace, whatever it costs me.

cores.belief: Other people's opinions decide my value.
cores.preferred: Opinions are information, not a verdict on me.
cores.protects: being caught off guard by criticism
cores.costs: a value that goes up and down with every opinion
rules: If someone disapproves, I've done something wrong.
I should check what others think before I decide.

cores.belief: The world isn't safe; I have to stay on guard.
cores.preferred: I can be careful where it's needed and relaxed where it's not.
cores.costs: a body that never fully rests
rules: If I relax, something will go wrong.
I should always expect the worst.

cores.belief: Something bad is coming.
cores.preferred: I don't know what's coming, and I can meet it when it does.
cores.costs: joy you don't let yourself feel
rules: If things are going well, I should brace.
I shouldn't get my hopes up.

cores.belief: Playing small keeps me safe.
cores.preferred: Small, real steps toward what I want are safe enough.
cores.costs: the life you'd actually like, postponed
rules: If I aim high, I'll be humiliated.
I should stay where I can't fail.

cores.belief: Change is dangerous.
cores.preferred: Change is how I grow, one step at a time.
cores.costs: staying where you've outgrown
rules: If it's unfamiliar, it's dangerous.
I should stick with what I know.

cores.belief: There isn't enough to go around.
cores.preferred: There is often more possible than I can see from here.
cores.costs: holding tight, so nothing has room to flow
rules: If someone else gets it, there's less for me.
I should hold on to what I have.

cores.belief: I can't change how my life goes.
cores.preferred: I can't control everything, but I can always choose my next step.
cores.protects: the effort and risk of trying
cores.costs: chances you don't take, because why try
rules: If it hasn't worked before, it won't work now.
I should accept how things are.

cores.belief: I have to control everything or it falls apart.
cores.preferred: I can hold my part and let the rest move.
cores.costs: exhaustion, and people who stop offering to help
rules: If I don't do it myself, it won't be done right.
If I let go, everything falls apart.

cores.belief: It only counts if it turns out the way I planned.
cores.preferred: What happens is feedback; every result teaches me something.
cores.costs: good results that still feel like failure
rules: If it doesn't turn out as planned, I failed.
If I don't get exactly what I aimed for, I got nothing.

cores.belief: What I do doesn't really matter.
cores.preferred: Small things I care about matter, here and now.
cores.costs: caring less, so life feels flatter
rules: If it won't change much, why bother?
I shouldn't care too much.

cores.belief: I'll be okay once something outside me changes.
cores.preferred: I can feel okay and act now, before anything changes.
cores.protects: facing what I could do today
cores.costs: waiting for a day that keeps moving
rules: I'll be okay once things change.
I should wait until the conditions are right.

cores.belief: The people I love will leave.
cores.preferred: Some people stay. And when someone goes, I'm still here.
cores.costs: clinging or keeping distance, so closeness never gets to feel safe
rules: If I'm not careful, they'll go.
I should keep them happy at all costs.

cores.belief: No one will really be there for me.
cores.preferred: I can let people show up, and tell them what helps.
cores.protects: hoping for care and not getting it
cores.costs: not asking, so the belief never gets tested
rules: If I have to ask, it doesn't count.
I should rely only on myself.

cores.belief: It's my job to keep everyone else okay.
cores.preferred: I can care about people without carrying their feelings for them.
cores.protects: guilt, and being the one who caused someone pain
cores.costs: exhaustion, quiet resentment, a life lived for others
rules: If someone is upset, I have to fix it.
I can't rest while someone else needs something.

cores.belief: What I want counts less than what others want.
cores.preferred: My wants get a vote too.
cores.protects: conflict and anger aimed at me
cores.costs: slowly losing track of what you even want
rules: If what I want causes friction, I should drop it.
Their plans come first.

cores.belief: I don't know who I am without them.
cores.preferred: I can stay close and still have a self of my own.
cores.costs: choices that stay borrowed
rules: If I choose differently, I betray them.
I should check with them before I know what I think.

cores.belief: People will use me if I let them.
cores.preferred: Most people aren't out to use me, and I can notice the few who are.
cores.costs: a guardedness that others read as coldness
rules: If I'm generous, I'll be taken advantage of.
I should keep my guard up until people prove themselves.

cores.belief: Showing what I feel isn't safe.
cores.preferred: Feelings, shared at the right size with the right people, bring people closer.
cores.costs: flatness, distance, and feelings that leak out sideways
rules: If I show what I feel, I'll lose control or respect.
I should keep it together, always.

cores.belief: I can't handle things on my own.
cores.preferred: I've handled hard things before. I can learn this one.
cores.costs: handing over decisions, and never building the evidence
rules: If it's hard, I need someone else to sort it.
I should avoid things I might not manage.

cores.belief: It has to be perfect, or it doesn't count.
cores.preferred: Finished and good enough is a real result.
cores.costs: procrastination, burnout, and no satisfaction
rules: If it isn't perfect, it doesn't count.
I should redo it until there's nothing to criticise.

cores.belief: When I get it wrong, I should pay for it.
cores.preferred: Mistakes call for repair, not punishment.
cores.costs: a harshness that makes change harder, not easier
rules: If I mess up, I should feel bad for a long time.
Being hard on myself keeps me in line.

cores.belief: I can't stand feeling uncomfortable.
cores.preferred: Discomfort comes in waves. I can ride one out for a few minutes, then choose.
cores.costs: the scroll, snack or drink loop, and unfinished things
rules: If I feel restless, I need something to fix it now.
If it gets hard, I should switch to something easier.

cores.belief: Feeling good is frivolous, or risky.
cores.preferred: Enjoying my life is part of living it well, not a distraction from it.
cores.protects: being caught off guard, or looking unserious
cores.costs: a life that is responsible and flat, with the pull ignored
rules: If I'm enjoying myself, I'm not being serious.
I shouldn't get too excited.

cores.belief: I have to be sure before I can move.
cores.preferred: I can move with what I know now and learn the rest on the way.
cores.protects: making the wrong call, and being caught out by the unknown
cores.costs: decisions postponed, questions that never close, and moving on put on hold until an answer that may never come
rules: If I don't fully understand it, I shouldn't act.
I can't move on until I know why.

cores.belief: My thoughts and feelings tell me how things really are.
cores.preferred: Thoughts, feelings and views are information I can test, not facts or orders.
cores.protects: the effort and dizziness of questioning your own mind
cores.costs: every passing fear or story gets to steer, and beliefs never get tested because they don't look like beliefs
rules: If it feels true, it is true.
My beliefs are just how things are.

cores.belief: Letting go of the pain would mean letting go of them.
cores.preferred: I can keep the bond and let the pain soften.
cores.protects: the loss feeling final, the sense of disloyalty, and the fear of forgetting
cores.costs: joy that feels like betrayal, and a life that stays on hold after a loss
rules: I should keep grieving to honour what I lost.
Moving on would be a betrayal.

cores.belief: If I accept something, I owe something.
cores.preferred: I can receive freely and give freely, without keeping a ledger.
cores.protects: dependence, obligation, and being in someone's debt
cores.costs: turned-down help, gifts that feel heavy, and relationships where you only ever give
rules: If I receive, I must repay quickly.
Giving is safer than receiving.

cores.belief: More effort is the only way to get more.
cores.preferred: The right effort matters more than the most effort.
cores.protects: having to choose what not to do, and the guilt of looking lazy
cores.costs: exhaustion, being spread thin, and the few things that matter getting no more time than everything else
rules: If I'm not working flat out, I'm not getting anywhere.
Everything I take on deserves my full effort.
